title: Meet get_by_role
brief:
Write a locator that matches **exactly one** element: the **Products** link in the shop's menu.

Type only the part after `page.` - the site wraps it in a real test that asserts the match count, and outlines whatever you matched in the shop panel.

Start with the top of the priority order. A link's role is `link`; its name is the text you can see.

checks.name: role
checks.label: You used get_by_role - the top of the priority order
checks.feedback: It matched, but with something other than a role locator. A CSS selector like `.shop-menu a:nth-child(2)` is tied to the page's shape; `get_by_role("link", name="Products")` is tied to what a user sees. Try the role version here.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: get_by_role takes the role first and the visible name second: get_by_role("role", name="...").

reveal:
Notice what you did **not** have to know: no id, no class, no position in the menu. You described the element the way a person would, and that description survives redesigns.

Now one trap worth meeting before the next challenge. Try `get_by_role("link", name="Cart")` in the same box and watch the count come back as **7**, not 1.

Name matching finds a **substring**, so `"Cart"` matches the menu's *Cart* link and every *Add to cart* link on the page. That is real Playwright behaviour, not a quirk of this shop - and `exact=True` is how you turn it off when you need to.
